messages:
jess: Quick heads-up — started seeing intermittent OOMs on the runtime when serving longer contexts (~8k tokens) after the v2.3 roll. Happens on one p3-16x instance, not all pods. No obvious leak in app metrics.

liam: ugh. any heap profiles or logs? which allocator are we running (jemalloc/tcmalloc)? :thinking_face:

jess: jemalloc. I grabbed the container logs — the kernel OOM killer shows the runtime process as the victim. No obvious spike before the kill, more like retained > RSS threshold.

igor: can you paste the output of malloc_stats_print or jemalloc stats if you have it? fragmentation tends to look like this when arenas proliferate.

jess: posting a short dump I pulled right after a restart:
```
allocated: 14.8G
active: 16.1G
mapped: 24.0G
metadata: 512M
pactive: 12
arenas: 24
chunk: 4M

# arena stats (summarized)
arena[0]: allocated 1.2G dirty 0.2G
arena[1]: allocated 1.1G dirty 0.3G
...
arena[23]: allocated 0.4G dirty 0.05G
```

maya: 24 arenas on a single worker seems high. Are we using per-thread arenas (default)? each thread can create its own arena and never return memory to OS, causes fragmentation.

liam: yes — default jemalloc behavior for high-concurrency workloads. Two quick probes: 1) run with MALLOC_CONF="narenas:4,lg_chunk:22" and 2) enable stats printing at SIGUSR1 (malloc_stats_print) so we can capture before kill.

jess: can do. running a canary with narenas=4 now. also adding MALLOC_CONF=percpu_arena:disabled per some docs.

igor: also try enabling jeprof (if compiled) to get sampled allocations across time. If that's heavy, capture after a steady-state run:
```sh
# inside container
export MALLOC_CONF="narenas:4,percpu_arena:disabled,lg_chunk:22"
./runtime --serve --profiling=on &
# trigger workload script
/bin/bench_long_context.sh
# on SIGUSR1 the process will print stats to stderr
kill -USR1 <pid>
```

jess: patch applied and canary running. initial results look promising — mapped dropped from 24G -> 17G after new config. keeping it under watch.

liam: nice. if that helps, we should consider shipping a default MALLOC_CONF in our runtime image for Dedicated / Private to mitigate noisy neighbor fragmentation. but we should measure perf impact on latency.

maya: one more angle: we saw in older traces that the KV cache growth (per-request key/value) sometimes keeps refs alive in long-lived arena allocations. Any chance the cache is holding onto big tensors?

jess: good call — I inspected cache sizes and found one path where a ~600MB prefix KV slice wasn't being evicted due to a key mismatch bug. fix incoming.

igor: that explains the sudden jumps. two mitigation paths: 1) patch cache eviction; 2) reduce arenas to cap retained broken-up memory footprint. both together should reduce OOM frequency.

sre-oncall: logging note — I'll add an alert that triggers when mapped > 85% of instance memory for > 30s so we can catch this earlier. also will add a runbook entry: how to trigger malloc_stats_print and how to roll a canary with MALLOC_CONF.

jess: thanks — I'll push the cache eviction PR and keep the canary running for 2 hours. will post the malloc_stats_print output if we see another bump.

liam: if the canary stabilizes, let's schedule a short perf run to ensure the MALLOC_CONF change doesn't add tail-latency regressions. also add a benchmark tag in the run so we can compare token throughput.

maya: SG. one more datapoint — if fragmentation persists after fixes, we should try the jemalloc decay_time and extent hooks; some customers saw benefit with decay_time=1.

jess: noted. thanks all. cc @igor for follow-up on profiling artifacts. :thumbsup:
